column1: # What the upstream-drift workflow watches, and the single source of truth for it.
# build/check-upstream.sh reads this; it knows how to query each ecosystem but nothing about which
# components this repository binds. Adding a native SDK means adding a row here.
# Columns are single-tab-separated.
#   group    reporting group - one GitHub issue per group, titled with this text
#   label    how the component is named inside the issue
#   kind     cocoapods | maven | github-release | github-tag | nuget
#   pin      the MSBuild property in Directory.Build.props holding the pinned version
#   locator  kind-specific: pod name, groupId:artifactId[:packaging][@repo], owner/repo, or the
#            NuGet package id
#   confirm  download URL template with {version}, or "-" to derive it from the locator
# github-tag rather than cocoapods (the pods exist: MarketingCloudSDK, MarketingCloud-AppGroupSDK):
# the tag archive is what FetchXcFrameworks.sh downloads, so the check confirms the thing the
# build consumes.
# The SFMC SDK core is the third thing that moves this package, and the only one no vendor index
# reports: SFMCSDK.Net.iOS is published from the sibling repository and pinned here by exact
# version, so a release there leaves this package resolving the older core with nothing to say so
# - which is exactly how the 4.0.1.2 re-pin came to be filed by hand. The `nuget` check is
# deliberately asymmetric: a pin BEHIND nuget.org is a finding (re-pin here and cut a binding
# revision), a pin AHEAD of it is the normal mid-flight state of a release train (the sibling
# publishes first) and is only logged.
#   source   owner/repo publishing the component - optional, and only meaningful on nuget
#            rows, where the drift finding links that repository's release notes for the
#            version it reports
# group
